newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls still set the pace on German share market.
newsitem.headline: Bulls still set the pace on German share market.

text.p: Bulls continued to prevail on the German share market in pre-bourse trade on Thursday, with the ever-rising dollar and a higher close on Wall Street fuelling further gains on the IBIS DAX index.
At 0711 GMT, the IBIS DAX index was up 50.67 points, or 1.16 percent, at 4,435.49 points, just shy of record levels, while the September DAX future was up 23.5 points at 4,443.5.

"This market is like a train moving full-steam ahead, which means it is going to take a while for it to slow down. We could lose of couple of hundred points and it would not make any difference," a Frankfurt trader said.
Another dealer said that it was predominantly foreign investment driving early gains. But one trader said that the importance of the domestic private investor should not be underestimated.

"A lot of private clients are seeing these records on television every night, they say to themselves that they want a piece of the action and are putting money into investment funds," the trader said.
"It looks like every prognosis at the start of the year for this market was way too conservative. This bull run is giving the analysts a real headache," he said.
As to whether or not the market is getting ready for a crash, dealers said that there was too much caution around.

"The word "crash" is on everyone's lips and people are saying the market is overheating. But look at the backdrop to this bull run -- low interest rates, weak mark -- and it's hard to see any evidence pointing to a real crash," he said.
Among individual sectors, focus was again on the banking sector which has chalked up monster gains in recent days.
Commerzbank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank were centre of attention after both banks reported their first half 1997 figures early on.
Commerzbank said that its operating profit after provisions was up 23.2 percent at 1.63 billion marks, which was above analysts' expectations.

Bayerische Vereinsbank, which said earlier this week that it plans to merge with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, saw its operating profit after provisions rise 15.2 percent to 765.7 million marks, somewhat below expectations.
Both shares had a rollercoaster ride pre-bourse.
Commerzbank was down 15 pfennigs at 64.45 marks, while Vereinsbank was down 30 pfennigs at 76.70 marks, but establishing a solid trend for bank stocks was difficult.
Dealers were also closely monitoring retailer Metro AG, which split its shares on Wednesday and led to some confusion and incorrect pricing.
Just before the end of electronic trade on Wednesday the bourse suspended trade in Metro and corrected the error in pricing.
Metro shares were down 2.32 percent at 92.80 marks pre-bourse.
